text:
maya (CS): hey team, customer reported duplicated completions when they hit an SSE disconnect and then retried. they see partial tokens, reconnect with resume headers, then a client retry spawns a second generation overlapping the resumed stream. attached logs and timestamps.

julia (Customer): repro steps I used:
1) open SSE to /v1/stream with session_id header.
2) receive ~5 tokens then connection drops.
3) client reconnects with Resume-Session: s_abc123 and Last-Event-ID: 23.
4) client waits ~10s then, timing out, issues a fresh POST /v1/generate with same prompt (no idempotency key).
Outcome: server resumes and sends events event_id 24..end, then separately sends a new generation events starting from 1..end -> duplicates in UI and doubled billing.

maya (CS): they say backoff is exponential but jitter is small; sometimes retry happens before server finishes persisting resume state.

kevin (Platform): can you paste headers and response event fields? are you setting an idempotency key on the POST?

julia (Customer): resume request headers:
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Resume-Session: s_abc123
Last-Event-ID: 23
Authorization: Bearer sk-...

POST retry headers:
POST /v1/generate
Idempotency-Key: <not-set>

Events include fields: session_seq, event_id, correlation_id in json payloads.

ravi (SRE): hypothesis: resume handshake is async. if resume commit to persistent state happens after the POST is accepted, server will run two independent flows: resumed stream continuing the prior job (using KV/prefix cache) and a concurrently created new job from POST -> duplicates.

maya (CS): timeline from customer logs: resume reconnect at 2025-10-02T15:12:08Z, POST accepted 15:12:11Z, resume commit to DB at 15:12:12Z. so POST got through before resume persisted. correlation-id 01GZ... included.

kevin (Platform): I'll try to reproduce with an artificial delay on resume-commit.

ravi (SRE): local repro steps:
- run server with ENV DEV_RESUME_COMMIT_DELAY_MS=1500
- start SSE, drop after 5 tokens
- reconnect immediately with Last-Event-ID 5
- client issues POST after 800ms
Observed: POST created job J123; later resume commit applied and resumed job R456; both emitted final completions -> duplicates.

kevin (Platform): mitigation ideas:
- short term: require Idempotency-Key on POSTs that might overlap with an active session (policy/SDK).
- server-side reservation token on resume handshake: issue a short-lived reservation that blocks new POSTs for N ms until resume commit done.
- longer term: make resume commit atomic before signaling resume. that will ensure resume always wins vs near-simultaneous POST.

maya (CS): customer can't enforce idempotency key for all clients (third-party integrators). need server-side fallback.

ravi (SRE): server-side proposals:
1) persistent session lock: on transport connect set session_state=RESUMING and reject incoming POSTs (409) until state=READY.
2) accept POSTs but use prompt-hash + resume markers to dedupe post-hoc. messy.
3) best: atomic commit during handshake so resume is guaranteed applied before any new POST job creation.

kevin (Platform): notes: we already have resume_state column. blocking handshake until commit can add latency for normal reconnects. alternative: use redis-based active_session_locks with CAS in POST handler to avoid schema migration.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: platform/resume-atomic-probe @ 1845006820 by kevin

ravi (SRE): quick hotfix I tested: on resume connect set key resume_pending:<session_id> = true in redis with TTL 5s. POST handler does GETSET or GET and if key exists returns 409 + Retry-After: 1s. TTL avoids permanent stuck state. works for repro. caveat: if resume fails to clear key we rely on TTL.

kevin (Platform): agree, redis lock seems low-risk and fast to roll out. add correlation-id logging and metric resume_conflict_count so we can measure incidence. also expose Retry-After header in SDKs.

maya (CS): billing concern: customer saw double billing. what do we do about credits?

ravi (SRE): options: detect duplicate completions via prompt-hash + session heuristics and issue credits for the second generation; or prevent duplicates proactively. we can run a backfill detection over last 48h and surface suspected dup cases for manual or automatic crediting.

kevin (Platform) - action items:
- implement redis resume_pending lock on resume connect (ravi) - hotfix
- update POST handler to honor lock and return 409 + Retry-After (kevin)
- emit metric resume_conflict_count and include correlation-id in spans (ravi)
- docs: update client best practices for resume+retry (maya)
- billing: run duplicate-detection backfill for last 48h and prepare credits (finance + cs)

maya (CS): i'll tell the customer. can we get the hotfix today? high priority for them.

kevin (Platform): deploying now, ETA ~45m. will post PR.

kevin (Platform): PR: https://git.redwood.ai/platform/pulls/512 implemented redis lock and 409 response.

alerts-bot: deployment platform/resume-atomic-probe succeeded in 3 regions at 1845006888 :rocket:

julia (Customer): testing now. when I attempted reconnect then immediate POST, POST returned 409 fast; client retried after 700ms and resume completed; no duplicates observed. looks good — thanks :relieved:

maya (CS): great. closing the loop and will open a billing ticket for potential credits if the customer had dup charges. i'll follow up once they confirm.

ravi (SRE): follow-ups: propose SDK change to surface Retry-After automatically and add Idempotency-Key recommendations. filed platform/SDK#217.

maya (CS): thanks all. tagging @kevin @ravi for postmortem notes and I'll file an internal incident if billing impact escalates.
